examples.solution_text:
$\theta$ is opposite the $12$ cm side; $28^{\circ}$ is opposite the $8$ cm side.
$\begin{align*}\frac{\sin\theta}{12}&=\frac{\sin28^{\circ}}{8}\\ \sin\theta&=\frac{12\sin28^{\circ}}{8}\end{align*}$
The calculator gives the acute angle.
$\alpha=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{12\sin28^{\circ}}{8}\right)=44.765542\ldots^{\circ}$
Since $\theta$ is obtuse, subtract the unrounded acute angle from $180^{\circ}$.
$\begin{align*}\theta&=180^{\circ}-44.765542\ldots^{\circ}\\ \theta&\approx135^{\circ}\end{align*}$

The angles opposite the $15$ cm side are $\angle AQC$ and $\angle APC$. Each has the same sine.
$\begin{align*}\frac{\sin\theta}{15}&=\frac{\sin24^{\circ}}{9}\\ \sin\theta&=\frac{15\sin24^{\circ}}{9}\end{align*}$
The acute angle is at $Q$.
$\begin{align*}\angle AQC&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{15\sin24^{\circ}}{9}\right)\\ \angle AQC&=42.679322\ldots^{\circ}\\ \angle AQC&\approx43^{\circ}\end{align*}$
The obtuse angle at $P$ is its supplementary angle.
$\begin{align*}\angle APC&=180^{\circ}-42.679322\ldots^{\circ}\\ \angle APC&\approx137^{\circ}\end{align*}$
Both triangles are valid: $24^{\circ}+42.679322\ldots^{\circ}<180^{\circ}$ and $24^{\circ}+137.320677\ldots^{\circ}<180^{\circ}$.
